text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato said in a message to Swiss right-wing leader that he was shocked about remarks Blocher made about Switzerland's role in World War Two in a public speech last Saturday. Blocher said that Switzerland did not need to apologise for any of its actions during that period.
- The Swiss government signed an agreement with Yugoslavia to send back some 12,000 Yugoslavians asylum seekers by the end of August.
- Jelmoli announced it will pay shareholders a dividend of 28 Swiss francs per share after having paid out none in 1996.

- Newtelco signed a contract to start an international partnership with Tele Danmark and British Telecom. Newtelco, founded by the Swiss Federal Railways, Migros and Union Bank of Switzerland, expects sales of one billion Swiss francs for the year.
- Swiss brewery Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann is shutting down subsidiary Baumberger Getraenke AG, a beverage maker.
- Switzerland imported 11.88 million tonnes of raw oil and oil products in 1996, an increase of 6.5 percent over 1995. Nearly 90 percent was imported from African countries.
